title: Say No
coreMove: Protective refusal is not rude withdrawal; it is how you keep your calendar, body, and attention free enough to honor the few yeses that deserve you.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who use focus language to bless one more yes
exampleSpecs.stakes: catch a polite sentence before it spends the hour
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Quinn notices that accepting one more proposal review would betray the protected yes

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose phones keep turning access into obligation
exampleSpecs.stakes: write a no before the next notification arrives
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Idris uses the Reviews.org phone-checking data to limit access

exampleSpecs.audience: people facing good opportunities that slowly take the work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maia's narrower scope stays calmer while Ruth's open scope gets brittle

exampleSpecs.audience: people who mistake no for coldness
exampleSpecs.stakes: reframe refusal as a hinge, not a wall
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Suki hears that a no can protect the right yes

exampleSpecs.audience: learners who think saying no means doing less
exampleSpecs.stakes: teach focus by cutting attractive extras
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben learns that fewer booths can ask for more care

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose environment needs to carry the no
exampleSpecs.stakes: show fewer openings leaving more attention for the care that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rafael closes nonurgent access so the live care channel gets his whole ear
